persona: One person who has marked a stack of short answers against a rubric by hand within the last year — a teacher, teaching assistant, tutor or exam marker — who did not build this page and has not had it explained to them. Deliberately narrow: the gate asks whether the person who owns this workflow can tell what the agent may and may not do, so a general software reader would answer a different question. Nobody has been screened against this description yet.

privacy: No participant identity or personal data is stored. The fixtures are synthetic and alias-only.
rerunProtocol: Screen for the persona above before anything else, in one question: 'When did you last mark a set of short answers against a rubric by hand?' If the answer is never, stop — the session would measure a different person's reaction.

Recruit between one and three people who pass that screen, did not build this page and have not had it explained to them. One is enough to run the gate; three is the ceiling. Ask for twenty minutes and consent to being quoted verbatim.
Ask Q1 and Q2 from docs/GATE-P2.md before the page is opened, and write the answers down as they are said.

Hand over docs/GATE-P2-BYHAND.md with the page closed. Say once: 'Find the answers you would want to look at twice before any of these marks went out.' Time it, and count the passes they make over the sheet. Record the ids they name and the ids they do not.

Open https://androlay.github.io/withheld/ and say exactly one sentence: 'This is a page for marking a class of short answers, and an AI agent can help with it.' Then ninety seconds of silence, no tour, no narration.

Repeat the same find-the-second-look task on the page, with a new timer, and record the ids again. Count the steps the same way: every click, every row opened, every view switched. The step count is the comparison that matters; the timings are context for it.
Ask Q3 and Q4, and record whether the participant said unprompted that the agent cannot score or release.

Write every answer verbatim into the Result section of docs/GATE-P2.md with the date, and copy both measures as 'one participant, one pile, N steps in X minutes by hand against M steps in Y minutes on the page'.
Copy anything the participant wanted that this page does not do into docs/PROGRESS.md as a work item.
reportingRules: One participant is not a rate. Two timings from one person on one pile are an anecdote with a number attached.
Report step counts as the two raw numbers, never as a ratio, a reduction or a percentage. Four steps against nine is a sentence; '56 % fewer steps' is an invention.
Never convert these results into a percentage, a speed-up, a saving per week, or any claim about markers in general.
If two or three sessions run, record each separately. Do not average them and do not write 'users found'.
Comprehension is the primary reading: whether the participant can say what the agent may not do without being told. A faster session with that answer wrong is a failed gate, not a mixed result.
A fail is a result and is more useful than a pass. Quote it in the words it was given.
notClaimed: No user comprehension, time saving, adoption, workload or impact result is claimed. The hosted browser run proves delivery, not that anyone outside the author has used this page.
